body.objective: Make result-to-atlas registration automatic and fail closed. Recent certified results emit valid per-result fragments under residual_atlas/, but the published overview consumes only six manually maintained canonical team fragments; the new polar cyclic-BV obstruction, counterflow all-Hodge shortfall and charged-time event-map theorem therefore remain absent from the shared atlas even though their evidence and fragments have landed.
body.stop_condition: Add a deterministic registry/coverage layer that discovers every committed atlas fragment, validates its schema and evidence hashes, resolves deliberate supersession, deduplicates entry IDs and proves that each publishable per-result fragment is represented exactly once in the canonical shared atlas. Either generate the six team aggregates from registered per-result fragments or let the overview consume the registry directly; do not require manual copy-paste into large generator files. Add `s-f coverage --kind atlas` (or an equivalent coordinator section) listing unregistered results, stale aggregate rows, duplicate/conflicting entries and missing paper links. Integrate this with the reverse result-to-paper coverage baseline and the evidence DAG. Demonstrate the three live missing rows named in the objective, preserve stable entry IDs and public-vs-working-tree typing, and add mutations for an unregistered fragment, duplicate ID with divergent scope, stale evidence hash, explicit supersession and uncommitted preview input.
body.forbid: no silent last-writer-wins merge; no treating an untracked preview as publishable; no duplicate result collapse without an explicit equivalence/supersession witness; no regeneration of scientific certificates; no requirement that each team hand-edit a monolithic aggregate; no weakening evidence-hash or claim-boundary checks
notes: 2026-07-21 live reproduction: residual_atlas/einstein-weyl-polar-ungauged-bv-residual-obstruction-fragment-v1.json is committed and validates, but build_residual_atlas.py reports 365 entries and consumes only bridge/einstein_sector/atlas/einstein-compact-product-atlas-fragment.json plus five other canonical aggregates; the new row is absent. The same registration gap applies to the latest counterflow all-Hodge and charged-time theorem fragments.
